selected_modules.reason: Primary localization target. The issue is explicitly a C++ modules ICE: summary says "ICE in check_return_expr from imported defaulted function", reproducer is in g++.dg/modules, and compiler paths point directly into C++ frontend files `gcc/cp/typeck.cc` (`check_return_expr`), `gcc/cp/semantics.cc`, `gcc/cp/method.cc`, `gcc/cp/decl2.cc`, and `gcc/cp/pt.cc`. Module docs say `gcc/cp` owns C++ semantics, templates, constexpr, and modules, matching the domain tags and stack locations.

Relevant shared front-end support. Issue facts mention `gcc/c-family/c-opts.cc` and options include module-related flags and warning handling (`-Wno-global-module`). The observed bad log likely reflects option mismatch in the harness, but the actual bug also includes a front-end diagnostic about conflicting global module declaration, so shared C-family option/pragma/diagnostic infrastructure is a plausible contributor around modules-related command handling and shared front-end behavior.

The bug includes both an ICE and a specific error diagnostic: `error: conflicting global module declaration ...`, and issue facts mention `gcc/diagnostic-global-context.cc:517`. While likely not the root semantic source, this module owns language-independent diagnostic emission and ICE reporting, so it is relevant for the immediate failure path and for any null/invalid state surfacing during reporting.

Useful upstream/shared IR candidate because C++ frontend semantic checks like return-expression validation, template instantiation, and defaulted function generation ultimately manipulate GCC tree nodes and declarations. The issue involves imported/defaulted functions, constexpr, and module-merged declarations, all of which can expose malformed or inconsistent tree state consumed by `gcc/cp` routines. This module is a reasonable shared substrate candidate if the frontend bug is triggered by corrupted declaration/tree representation rather than purely local C++ logic.
